detailSections.content:
D1. Two different failures, one fix programme (K1, K2, K8).
The enforcement model names the target precisely: "a run that stops with pending tasks because the primary agent judged itself finished" (enforcement-model.md:3-8). But the implemented mechanism is a veto: the guard refuses to let the run write COMPLETE while work remains. It never compels another cycle. The spike states the asymmetry outright — "No Stop hook, so the guard must be invoked ... a primary that skips the call is indistinguishable from one that obeys a verdict it never checks" (enforcement-evaluator-spike.md:184-188). So the programme fixed "cannot lie about being done" while leaving "cannot choose to stop" untouched.

  false completion:  [guard exit 2] -> COMPLETE write refused        (mechanized)
  mid-plan stop:     [turn ends]   -> nothing re-enters the loop     (not mechanized)

D2. Why status-only enforcement is the linchpin (K3).
loop-guard.mjs is deliberately status-only: outstanding work = any non-terminal task, non-empty control.activeTasks, or non-terminal lifecycle. It answers "is work left in the record?", never "is the evidence good?". Two consequences:
- A run that bulk-marks tasks completed makes the guard exit 0, so the close-out pattern observed here is indistinguishable, to the guard, from genuine completion.
- The guard must be invoked; nothing outside the loop can force it. A run that simply ends its turn skips even the veto.
This is why the 36/16-task close-out could be written in one commit with a post-dated journal row and still produce exit 0.

D3. Postmortem: what the durable record actually shows (K4, K5).
Plan-Control state at 6604936^ for both large plans:

  currentState : NOT_STARTED
  cycle        : 0
  lastCheckpoint: "none"
  lastModelRun : ""
  status       : "ready"
  tasks        : 36/36 (or 16/16) pending
  nextTransition: "On a future explicit csm-build invocation, NOT_STARTED -> RECOVER"

Then 6604936 (2026-09-27T23:15:28Z) rewrote both plans: all tasks completed, status complete, plus one journal row {transition: "NOT_STARTED -> COMPLETE", timestamp: "2026-09-27T23:20:00Z"} — after the commit. No .agents/csm-build-state/*.json or .agents/builds/*.json exists for either slug, while ~30 commits carrying T001..T016 landed in 2026-09-27 alone with multi-hour gaps. Plans that DID reach COMPLETE (enforce-trace-emission, enforcement-closure, session-lifecycle) show cycle-1 journal rows sharing a single timestamp and empty task refs, and lastModelRun still naming the planning run — backfilled, not live.

D4. The design-side contribution from csm-plan (K6).
csm-plan is intentionally a planner: "Every implementation task must remain pending when the plan is saved" and "SAVED is the terminal planning state ... end the response without asking whether to start work". A genuine deferral becomes a blocked task, and blocked is non-terminal for the guard, so a plan containing a blocked task can never be driven to COMPLETE by any amount of looping. No continuation/run budget exists in csm-plan. The net is that csm-plan optimizes for verifiability and resumability, and leaves autonomous completion entirely to csm-build — which has no driver.

D5. Other terminators that compound the stop (K7).
- scripts/lib/agent-session-executor.mjs: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 min; on timeout it returns failed/timeout and does not resume the session.
- csm-orchestrate: remainderPolicy defaults to { maxRemainders: 0 }; a hard node failure persists a resumable supersession pointer and fails closed (after ≤2 retries).
- Context exhaustion: "harness-managed by automatic compaction; if it still occurs it is a non-quota fatal surfaced to the primary" — a hard stop with no run-level continuation.
- tmux bootstrap: on an interactive human CLI not already in tmux, it launches a detached session and ends the original invocation (a hand-off, not a mid-plan stop, but it does mean the invoking turn does no build work).

D6. The harness seam that can actually fix it (K9).
The repo's premise ("nothing outside the loop can enforce") is a capability claim that is falsified by the installed toolchain. opencode 1.15.12 exposes:
- the session.idle event in the documented plugin event list, and a plugin event hook plus an SDK client ("client: An opencode SDK client for interacting with the AI");
- a global plugin directory (~/.config/opencode/plugins/) and a plugin config option;
- compaction.auto (default true) and the experimental compaction hooks, including experimental.compaction.autocontinue, which fires "after compaction succeeds and before a synthetic user auto-continue message is added" (skip by setting enabled=false).
No plugin is configured in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc today. A csm continuation plugin — on session.idle, locate the active run's durable cursor, run the deterministic guard, and if it exits 2 with a non-blocked/non-paused status, inject a continuation prompt — is the concrete "Stop hook" substitute. This is unverified end-to-end (types/docs only), so it is recorded as a pilot, not a proven fix.

Causal chain, one line: no host-side re-entry (K1,K9) + prose-only continue (K2) + status-only guard (K3) -> runs end at a turn boundary with work remaining -> the durable cursor is not the driver (K4,K5) -> the user becomes the loop.

executiveSummary.content:
This finding answers why csm-plan/csm-build runs stopped partway on 2026-09-26..27 and required the user to say "continue" repeatedly, even though the plans eventually landed. Two distinct problems were being conflated in the fix programme: (A) a run that falsely claims completion while tasks remain, and (B) a run that stops while tasks remain but never claims completion. The repo's enforcement work solves (A) well and (B) almost not at all.

Pipeline of the failure:

  model finishes a csm-build cycle
      -> emits a final assistant message (turn boundary)
      -> opencode: no Stop hook / no forced re-entry (by default)
      -> loop-guard can only exit 0/2 and veto a COMPLETE write
      -> nothing re-enters the loop
      -> user must prompt "continue"
      -> (repeat)

The strongest evidence is the empirical postmortem. For the 36-task plan (2026-09-26-system-remediation-jev-embedding) and the 16-task plan (2026-09-27-remaining-work-continuous-run), the plan Control never left currentState=NOT_STARTED, cycle=0, lastCheckpoint="none", lastModelRun="" with every task pending, right up to the close-out commit 6604936 at 2026-09-27T23:15:28Z; that commit flipped all tasks to completed and the plan to complete, and a synthetic journal row was stamped 2026-09-27T23:20:00Z, roughly five minutes AFTER the commit. No csm-build-state record exists for either plan. Work nonetheless landed as ~30 commits across two days, with multi-hour gaps between them — the signature of repeated manual re-prompting, not one continuous run. The successor plan's own goal says it plainly: complete ALL remaining work in ONE continuous csm-build run without stopping, because "the user asked for one go without stopping".

Headline caveats. The work was independently verified via .agents/evidence/completion/final-verdict.json, so "no csm-build-state" does not mean the output was unverified. And the repo's foundational premise — "opencode has no Stop hook, so the decision cannot be enforced from outside the loop" — is too strong as a capability statement: opencode 1.15.12 exposes session.idle events, an SDK client for injecting prompts, and compaction hooks, so external continuation is unconfigured, not impossible.

keyFindings.content:
K1. supported — The csm-build loop cannot survive a turn boundary. opencode provides no forced-continuation by default; the deterministic loop guard only vetoes a COMPLETE claim (exit 0/2) and has no facility to restart a turn. [ref-enforcement-model, ref-evaluator-spike, ref-loop-guard]

K2. supported — The "Do not stop after one task or cycle" rule is prose-only. Positive continuation is never mechanized; only false completion is blocked by code (assertCompletionGate, defined in loop-guard.mjs, called from completeBuild). [ref-build-skill, ref-loop-guard, ref-build-state]

K3. supported — The guard is status-only, so a run that flips every task to completed (or writes status=complete) makes it exit 0. The repo admits the guard "cannot detect a task marked completed with failing or fabricated evidence". This is the linchpin gap: false completion is only partially blocked, and mid-plan stops are not blocked at all. [ref-evaluator-spike, ref-loop-guard]

K4. supported — For the two large Sep 26/27 plans, csm-build never drove a persistent loop. Plan Control stayed NOT_STARTED / cycle 0 / lastCheckpoint "none" / lastModelRun "" with all tasks pending until one close-out commit bulk-flipped them; the terminal journal row is timestamped after the commit; no csm-build-state record exists for either plan. [ref-plan-jev-embedding, ref-plan-remaining, ref-commit-closeout, ref-final-verdict]

K5. partially-supported — The durable per-cycle cursor/resume contract was not maintained on these runs, and even plans that did reach COMPLETE backfilled their journals: cycle-1 rows share one exact timestamp with empty placeholder task refs, and acceptance evidence was authored at plan-creation time rather than as execution receipts. (Scoped: older runs such as dynamic-worker-runtime do carry live cursors, so this is not a universal abandonment.) [ref-plan-enforce-trace, ref-plan-enforcement-closure, ref-plan-session-lifecycle]

K6. supported — csm-plan contributes by design to non-autonomous completion: it saves with every task pending and status ready, defines a genuine deferral as a blocked task that cannot be closed without a user decision, and models no continuation or run budget. Plans are resumable and verifiable, but not autonomously completable. [ref-plan-skill, ref-plan-loopeval]

K7. supported — Additional structural terminators shorten runs: the agent-session executor imposes a 15-minute timeout with no auto-resume; csm-orchestrate defaults maxRemainders to 0 and fails closed on a node failure (after at most 2 retries); context exhaustion is a non-quota fatal surfaced to the primary. [ref-agent-session-executor, ref-orchestrate-recovery, ref-orchestrate-skill, ref-build-skill, ref-context-mgmt]

K8. supported — The prior fix programme targeted false completion and mechanized only that. The repo's own docs record evaluator efficacy as a CONDITIONAL GO and obedience-only enforcement as NO-GO/unproven, with the deterministic (status-only) guard carrying the weight; the mid-plan stop has no fixed mechanism. [ref-enforcement-model, ref-evaluator-spike, ref-prior-research, ref-prior-meta]

K9. recommendation — opencode 1.15.12 exposes the missing continuation surface: plugins can observe session.idle and are handed an SDK client, plus compaction hooks and compaction.auto=true. A global plugin that re-enters a csm run while its durable guard reports work remaining is the implementable replacement for the absent Stop hook. [ref-opencode-plugins, ref-opencode-config, ref-opencode-sdk-types]

K10. recommendation — Make the durable cursor the driver: gate completion on a live per-cycle checkpoint cadence and per-task execution receipts (not bulk status flips), and have csm-plan emit a completion contract with phased driver tasks (independent verdict -> commit -> push/CI -> close) so a bounded, resumable unit of work is what a session is asked to finish. [ref-loop-guard, ref-plan-skill, ref-plan-remaining]

processAppendix.content:
Tier: DEEP. Source mode: hybrid (repository reads + vendor docs). Run started 2026-09-28T00:34Z.

Triage: the question concerns the behavior and design of two in-repo skills, so it is answerable principally from the repository, with external vendor documentation needed to test the repo's "no Stop hook" premise. Four research tracks were dispatched in parallel: (1) csm-plan/csm-build skill text and code — stopping affordances and completion enforcement; (2) artifact postmortem of 2026-09-26..27; (3) harness/turn-boundary reality; (4) prior-art and completed fixes. Independently, the primary retrieved the opencode plugins/config docs.

Challenge (adversarial, anti-anchored). Core verdicts:
- C1 (no continuation possible): DOWNGRADE. The mechanism is right (guard cannot restart a turn), but the impossibility premise is falsified — opencode 1.15.12 exposes session.idle, the plugin event hook + SDK client, and experimental.compaction.autocontinue. Corrected claim adopted: nothing external forces continuation by default; it is unconfigured, not impossible.
- C2 (prose-only continue): UPHELD; locator corrected (assertCompletionGate defined in loop-guard.mjs, called from state.mjs).
- C3 (plans never advanced; bulk close-out): UPHELD; count precision corrected (one synthetic terminal row per plan, timestamped after the commit; independent verification layer exists).
- C4 (no live cursor): UPHELD with downgrades — task refs are empty/placeholder rather than broken; acceptance evidence predates execution (verify at plan creation, not commit 9981006); scope limited (not universal).
- C5 (csm-plan designs for non-autonomous completion): UPHELD (nuance: blocked tasks are resolvable by later evidence, not only user decisions).
- C6 (other structural terminators): UPHELD with downgrades — tmux is a hand-off; context exhaustion is a non-quota fatal, not "non-resumable"; orchestrate retries nodes ≤2 before failing closed.
- C7 (prior fixes target false completion): DOWNGRADE — the docs name premature stopping as the target, but only false-completion blocking is mechanized. Corrected claim adopted.
- Missing claim supplied: the guard is status-only, so bulk status flips defeat it (adopted as K3 / linchpin).

recommendation.content:
Recommendation: treat mid-plan stopping as a host-integration bug, not an instruction-wording bug, and fix it in three layers, cheapest and highest-leverage first.

1. Implement a continuation supervisor at the opencode plugin seam (highest leverage; recommended to pilot first). A global plugin (~/.config/opencode/plugins/, or a plugin entry in opencode.json) subscribes to session.idle; on idle it locates the active csm run from the durable record, runs the skill's own deterministic guard (csm-build/lib/loop-guard.mjs), and when the guard exits 2 and the control status is neither blocked nor paused, injects a bounded continue prompt via the plugin's SDK client. Safety rails: a per-run continuation budget (e.g. max injected continues) and a no-progress detector (stop if the record digest is unchanged across two continuations) so the plugin cannot spin. Confidence: the capability surface is documented (session.idle, client, compaction hooks); the end-to-end effect is unverified — pilot on one plan and measure stops per run before adopting. Cost of being wrong: a runaway loop is bounded by the budget/digest guard, so the downside is a paused run, not damage.

2. Make the durable cursor the driver, and stop accepting status flips as completion (csm-build + corpus gate). Require a live checkpoint cadence: each cycle must advance Control (cycle, lastCheckpoint, lastModelRun) with a journal row whose timestamp and task refs are real; completion must carry per-task execution receipts (command, exit code, artifact digest, bound task ID), not planning-time acceptance prose. Extend the corpus/lineage gate to fail a plan whose tasks are completed while the cursor never advanced past NOT_STARTED or whose completionReview is null. This directly kills the 6604936 pattern. Existing code already has the primitives (validatePlanLineage, recordEvaluatorReceipt); the missing piece is a cursor-advancement/evidence-binding predicate. Also treat the 15-minute agent-session timeout as a checkpoint-and-resume (re-invoke) rather than a terminal failed result when the guard reports work remaining.

3. Give csm-plan a completion contract and phase large plans (csm-plan). Add to each plan: (a) a declared continuation policy (session unit, checkpoint cadence, expected cycles, and the exact guard command a supervisor should run); (b) a machine-checkable completion contract (what "done" means at plan level, and the mandatory close-out task sequence: independent verdict -> authorized commit -> push/CI-green -> close), mirroring what the last plan had to invent ad hoc as T013-T016; (c) phase boundaries for large plans so a session is asked to finish a bounded, independently closable unit rather than 36 tasks at once; and (d) an up-front enumeration of any blocked/user-decision tasks so a plan is not silently undriveable. Optionally reduce reliance on blocked tasks by turning product decisions into explicit, answered decision points during planning.

Validation questions and thresholds: does stops-per-run fall from >1 to 0 on a representative 16-task plan with the supervisor on? Does the corpus gate reject a simulated bulk close-out (all tasks completed, cursor at cycle 0)? Does a resumed session reconstruct state solely from Control/journal/receipts? Rollback: the plugin is global config and removable by deleting one file; the gate change is per-task revertible; the plan-contract change is additive and /1 plans remain valid.

What would change this recommendation: if a controlled pilot shows the plugin's session.idle injection does not actually re-enter the loop (or the harness drops synthetic turns), then fall back to an external driver (a process that re-runs 'opencode run' while the guard exits 2) — which the repo already has a primitive for in scripts/lib/agent-session-executor.mjs, currently bounded at 15 minutes and without auto-resume.

tldr.content: csm-build did not fail to plan, and it did not fail to verify; it failed to keep driving. The mid-plan stop is a harness turn-boundary, not a model-quality bug: opencode exposes no forced-continuation by default, the skill's "do not stop" rule is prose-only, and the deterministic loop guard can only veto a false COMPLETE — it cannot restart a stopped turn. On 2026-09-26/27 the two large plans sat at NOT_STARTED / cycle 0 while ~30 commits landed across many separate sittings, then were bulk-marked complete in a single close-out commit. Fix it at the host seam (an opencode plugin that re-enters csm-build while the guard reports work remaining), make the durable cursor — not task status — the driver, and give csm-plan a completion contract.

unverifiedClaims.content:
U1. Whether the proposed session.idle -> client prompt continuation actually re-enters the agent loop in opencode 1.15.12. Only type declarations and vendor docs were read; no plugin was executed. Verify by piloting one continuation plugin on a single plan and observing whether a second cycle runs.

U2. The exact number of user re-prompts on 2026-09-26/27. No live transcript exists in the repo; the count is inferred from commit clustering (multi-hour gaps) and trace gaps. Verify only with the user's session history.

U3. Whether any task marked completed at the close-out was actually unbuilt. The independent final-verdict.json asserts all 36 signals were re-run and passed at HEAD, but this run did not reproduce the re-runs (read-only mandate) and the verdict is a separate ledger, not written into the plan cursor.

U4. Whether the earlier COMPLETE plans' journals were live or backfilled. The shared-timestamp and empty-task-ref pattern is strong evidence of backfill, but without a live trace of those runs the alternative (genuine same-instant journaling) cannot be excluded.

U5. The full set of factors behind the specific turn ends (context limit vs. self-judged stop vs. tmux hand-off). The mechanical capability gap is proven; the proximate cause of each individual stop is inferred.

U6. Whether the "opencode has no Stop hook" statement should be read as literal (no hook literally named Stop) or as a claim that no external continuation exists. The toolchain evidence supports the former and contradicts the latter as a capability statement, but the maintainers' intent is not recorded.

title: Why CSM plans were not built to completion and how to make csm-plan/csm-build finish (2026-09-26..27)
